title: nanobind wrappers: typed signatures, Boost-compatible argument names and exceptions, and path filenames
body:
#### Reference Issue

Part of #9601. This PR also contains what were #9593 (return types), #9609 (per-module parameter commits), #9594 (argument names, exception types and single registrations) and #9598 (filename paths and the stream read check). They are combined because RDKit's CI runs one pull request at a time; the commits keep the split.

#### What does this implement/fix? Explain your changes.

The nanobind wrappers (`RDK_BUILD_NANOBIND_WRAPPERS`) type many Python-facing arguments and return values as `nb::object`, `nb::tuple`, `nb::list` or `nb::dict`, so the generated signatures say `SMILES: object` or `-> tuple`, and arguments accept any type at the call boundary. The wrappers also differ from the Boost wrappers in some argument names, exception types and filename handling. This PR gives the nanobind wrappers accurate signatures and closes those gaps. #9613, which builds on it, generates type stubs from these signatures.

**Parameters** follow the rule in #9601 and how each argument is used:

| the argument is | type | renders as |
| --- | --- | --- |
| serialized text: SMILES, SMARTS, Mol/TPL/Mrv/XYZ/PDB/CDXML/ChemDraw/Mol2/SCSR blocks, SVG, sequences, JSON, the suppliers' text and MolStandardize's transform data | `StringOrBytes` | `str \| bytes` |
| a filename: the readers, suppliers and writers, `BuildFeatureFactory`, the cube-file reader and writer, `GetFingerprintsForMolsInFile`, the ChemDraw file readers | `std::filesystem::path` | `str \| os.PathLike` |
| only iterated | `PyIterableOf<T>` | `Iterable[T]` |
| indexed or measured with `len()` | `PySequenceOf<T>` | `Sequence[T]` |
| a list or dict filled in place for the caller | `PyListOf<T>`, `PyDictOf<K, V>` | `list[T]`, `dict[K, V]` |
| a list overwritten by index, so its initial elements can be any type | `PyOutputList` | `list[Any]` |
| converted to a `std::map` | `std::map<K, V>` | `Mapping[K, V]` |
| a callback (substructure match checks, lazy pickers' `distFunc`, SynthonSpace search callbacks and conformer generators, tautomer scoring) | `nb::typed<nb::callable, R(Args...)>` | `Callable[[Args...], R]` |
| `None` or a value (options, generators, molecules, sequences, NumPy transforms) | `std::optional<T>` or `T *` | `T \| None` |

**Return values** name their element types, including nested ones: `RingInfo.AtomRings` becomes `-> tuple[tuple[int, ...], ...]`, `SplitMolByPDBResidues` becomes `-> dict[str, Mol]`, and NumPy-backed returns become `numpy.ndarray[dtype=uint8, shape=(*)]`. Functions that can return `None` render `-> Mol | None` (or `Atom`, `Bond` or `ChemicalReaction`) through a `Nullable<Pointer>` return type in `Wrap_nb.h`: the parsers (`MolFromSmiles`, `MolFromMolBlock`, `AtomFromSmarts` and the rest), the suppliers' `__next__` and `__getitem__`, `GetBondBetweenAtoms`, `ReplaceCore`, `ReplaceSidechains`, `molzip`, `ReactionFromRxnFile`, `MCSResult.queryMol` and `SubstructLibrary.GetMol`, among others. Returns that are genuinely polymorphic keep `nb::object`. nanobind does not check return annotations, so they change no runtime behavior.

**Signatures name types from other modules.** nanobind renders a type by its C++ name, such as `RDKit::FingerprintGenerator<unsigned long long>`, until the module that registers it is imported. `rdMolProcessing`, `rdSynthonSpaceSearch`, `rdSubstructLibrary`, `rdMolDraw2D`, `rdForceField`, `rdSimDivPickers` and `pyAvalonTools` import the modules whose types their signatures name, as `rdForceFieldHelpers` already imports `rdForceField`.

`StringOrBytes`, its `pyObjectToString` helper (defined identically in `rdmolfiles.cpp` and `rdChemReactions.cpp`), `Nullable` and the container aliases live in `Wrap_nb.h`.

What changes for callers, beyond the signatures:

- **Other types are rejected at the call boundary.** A container or options object of the wrong kind raises `TypeError` instead of `RuntimeError: std::bad_cast` part-way through, which is what the Boost wrappers raise in most of these cases. `SynthonSpace.FingerprintSearch` crashed when `fingerprintGenerator` was not a fingerprint generator, and raises `TypeError` too.
- **Generators are accepted wherever an argument is only iterated.** `RenumberAtoms` and `SubstanceGroup.AddBracket` validate a length, and measured it with `len()` before converting; they now measure the converted vector, and raise the same errors. `BCUT2D` accepts any iterable of atom props: it registers the overload taking a property name first, so a `str` still selects that one. Where a wrapper keeps pointers to the elements after iterating, a generator can still crash it; #9611 fixes those.
- **`bytes` is accepted wherever the Boost wrappers take it.** Boost.Python converts a `std::string` argument from `str` or `bytes`, while nanobind's caster takes `str` alone, so every argument holding serialized text takes `StringOrBytes`. `MolFromXYZFile` and the Mrv and CDXML reaction file readers keep taking `str` alone: they take a `const char *`, which Boost.Python converts from `str` only.
- **Filenames take `bytes` and `os.PathLike`.** nanobind's `std::string` caster accepts only `str`, while the Boost wrappers accept all three. For the suppliers and writers it was worse than a type mismatch: `bytes` and `Path` missed the `std::string` overload and reached the file-object overload, so `ForwardSDMolSupplier` hung on either, `SDMolSupplier`, `SmilesMolSupplier` and `SDWriter` opened a file named `b'...'`, and `SmilesWriter`, `TDTWriter`, `PDBWriter` and `MaeWriter` raised `ValueErrorException`. The path overloads are registered ahead of the file-object overloads, and every use converts with `.string()`, since a path converts implicitly to `std::string` only where `path::string_type` is `std::string`, which is not the case on Windows.
- **A stream that cannot read is rejected.** `ForwardSDMolSupplier(42)` wrapped the `int` in a `streambuf`, and the parser then waited forever for an end of file. `python_streambuf_nb.h` raises `ValueError` at construction when the object has no `read`, with the message `MaeMolSupplier` already used; #9615 does the same for the Boost stream.
- **Arguments the Boost wrappers name are named.** The `Point2D`, `Point3D` and `PointND` methods (`AngleTo`, `SignedAngleTo`, `DotProduct`, `CrossProduct`, `DirectionVector`) take `other`, `ComputeGridCentroid` takes `grid`, `pt` and `windowRadius`, and `Atom.SetNoImplicit` takes `what`, so they can be passed by keyword. `SetNoImplicit`'s docstring had been joined onto the argument name, so it had none. `ComputeL1Norm` is left alone: `RealValueVect` and `DiscreteValueVect` share the name, and only the `DiscreteValueVect` overload names its arguments.
- **Value and index errors are the builtin types.** `rdBase` registered `ValueErrorException` and `IndexErrorException`, and `rdMIF` registered the same two C++ types again as `MIFValueError` and `MIFIndexError`, so importing `rdMIF` changed what every other module raised. Both are translated to `ValueError` and `IndexError`, as the Boost wrappers do, and an `IndexError` carries the index as `args[0]`. Exceptions with a C++ class of their own, such as `MolSanitizeException`, keep their Python types.
- **`MolFromMolBlock`, `MolFromMolFile` and `HasPropQueryBond` are registered once**; each was bound twice, so its docstring listed the same signature twice. `SmilesMolSupplier` keeps the argument name `data`, which the Boost wrapper uses, so `SmilesMolSupplier(fileName=...)` no longer works under nanobind.
- **`MrvWriterParams` is bound**, so the `params` overloads of `MolToMrvBlock` and `MolToMrvFile` can be called. Neither wrapper set bound it before.
- **`GenerateDepictionMatching2DStructure(mol, ref, -1, None, True)` works.** The untyped `params` overload accepted the bool and then failed to cast it, raising `RuntimeError`; the call now reaches the overload taking `acceptFailure`, as it does with the Boost wrappers.
- **`None` works where the Boost wrappers accept it**: `DrawMoleculeWithHighlights`' maps, `MolzipParams.setAtomSymbols`, `DoubleCubicLatticeVolume.GetPartialSurfaceArea`/`GetPartialVolume`, `DrawMolecule`'s two highlight lists, `SubstanceGroup.SetAtoms`/`SetBonds`/`SetParentAtoms`, which empty their list for it, and `molzipFragments`, which returns `None`. The params classes' `__setattr__` is registered to accept `None`, and the setters that clear a list for it take it: `rdShapeAlign.ShapeInputOptions.atomSubset` and `notColorAtoms`, `ShapeInput.shift`, `rdGaussianShape.ShapeInputOptions.atomSubset` and `SynthonSpaceSearchParams.excludedVolume`. Other attributes still reject `None` in their own setters.
- **`FindAtomEnvironmentOfRadiusN` accepts its `atomMap` dict**; it raised `TypeError` before.
- **Two arguments now reject what they silently mishandled.** `RingInfo.AddRing(None, ...)` dereferenced a null vector and raises `TypeError`, and `RGroupDecomposition.GetMatchingCoreIdx` raises `TypeError` for a `matches` argument that is not a list, instead of ignoring it.

Apart from wrong types rejected at the call boundary and the `fileName` keyword above, every input the nanobind wrappers accepted before is still accepted. `SynthonSpace.SubstructureSearch`'s line-range form is registered twice, once taking all five arguments and once taking `startLine` and `finishLine` by keyword after defaulted parameters, because a single Python signature cannot put required parameters after defaulted ones. The changed functions were called with the inputs that matter for each (lists, tuples, NumPy arrays, generators, `bytes`, paths, file objects, `None` and wrong types) under both wrapper sets, before and after.

#### Any other comments?

Some parameters stay `nb::object` because their type does not follow from how they are used: arguments written back into, arguments that take more than one kind of value, and ignored arguments. #9601 lists them.

`RDK_BUILD_NANOBIND_WRAPPERS` defaults to `OFF`, and this pull request changes no Boost wrapper.

Tests: where a change is observable from Python, the module's test file gains a test, run under both wrapper sets where the file is shared, and assertions that hold only under nanobind are guarded by `rdBase._wrapperType`. Each fails against a build without its change and passes with it, except one in `rough_test.py` that asserts generators are still accepted where they always were; `testSupplierAndWriterFilenamesAcceptPathLike` hangs rather than failing without its change. `Code/GraphMol/nbWrap/testTyping.py`, which is nanobind only, holds the signature assertions, parsing each overload's `__nb_signature__` with `ast`; one runs a fresh interpreter to check that signatures name types from other modules.

The branch was built locally with all optional modules. Every changed wrapper file that the `Ubuntu_x64_nb` job compiles passes GCC with that job's `-Wall -Wextra -Werror`, as well as clang. These pass:

- `Code/GraphMol/nbWrap/testTyping.py`: 4 tests and 25 subtests.
- `Code/GraphMol/nbWrap/rough_test.py`, which is nanobind only, with `testMolBundles1` deselected.
- The other 74 Python test files the nanobind build registers, apart from the local failures below.

Some tests abort or hang in local builds, with or without these changes (see #9601): `testMolBundles1`; `FilterCatalog`'s `test0FilterCatalogEntry`, `test2FilterCatalogTest` and `testFunctionalGroupHierarchy`; seven `SubstructLibrary` tests; `SynthonSpaceSearch`'s `testBestHit` and `testShapePossibleHitsWrite`, and `testShapeInterimFile`, which hangs; four `testEnumerations.py` tests; the serialization tests `testGeneralizedSubstruct.py`'s `test6Serialization` and `test7GenericMatchers`, `testPickleScaffoldNetwork.py`'s `test1Pickle` and `TautomerQuery`'s `test_serialization`; and destroying a `MolDraw2DSVG` under Boost. `testChemDraw.py`'s `test_cdxml` fails on this branch because it calls a function neither wrapper set registers; #9597 fixes that test.
